overview: This Senate resolution calls the annual Army-Navy football game, played between the U.S. Military Academy at West Point and the U.S. Naval Academy, "America's Game" and a key influence on military recruiting. It states the Senate's view that the game should be the only college football game broadcast during its time slot on the second Saturday of December, and that broadcasters, athletic conferences and colleges should avoid scheduling games against it. It also asks federal agencies to review their policies to better coordinate around and promote the game. As a "sense of the Senate" resolution, it expresses an opinion and does not have the force of law. The Senate approved it on February 25, 2026.
for: Supporters say the Army-Navy game is a unique tradition that honors service members and inspires future ones, and it deserves the nation's full attention without competing games.
against: Critics say Congress should not weigh in on college sports scheduling or television decisions, and the resolution has no legal effect in any case.
